Scans are 600 x 874 pixels. Parse OCR has many errors; about 0.069 of Britannica tokens are outside the vocabulary.
Parse looped on 2 scans (a blank cover and an engraved plate) and hit its token limit. These scans have no extracted text.

The first match run accepted list pages ("Coinage", "Willin'") that lack "(disambiguation)" in the title. The repaired rule removes pages that open with "may refer to". When the right article is not a BM25 candidate ("Coining (mint)"), the entry now has no match.
OCR-damaged headwords get a dictionary variant only when one close word exists (PHILLOOGY -> philology). Ambiguous damage (WILLIN) and damage below the 0.85 ratio still break search and matching.
The lexical rule still accepts wrong senses with the same title ("Naxos (Crete)" for the Aegean island).
